purpose: Official, version-sensitive evidence for model adapters. Vendor quality language is excluded from capability claims.

method.access: All URLs returned HTTP 200 on 2026-07-24. Documentation pages were read as rendered public HTML; YouTube items were confirmed through public oEmbed metadata only.
method.boundary: official_verified proves only the cited documentation claim at the access date. official_video_metadata proves that the official tutorial exists, not its full narrated content.

sources.title: Video generation with Sora | OpenAI API

claims.paraphrase: The Sora 2 video models and Videos API are deprecated and scheduled to shut down on 2026-09-24.
claims.boundary: Applies to the model/API names listed on the page.

claims.paraphrase: The API documents prompt generation, first-frame image reference, reusable non-human character assets, extensions, targeted edits, asynchronous polling and webhooks.
claims.evidence_locator: overview, image reference, characters, extensions, edits, webhooks
claims.boundary: Each feature has separate constraints; not every combination is allowed.

claims.paraphrase: The guide documents 16- and 20-second generations, Sora 2 Pro 1080p portrait/landscape exports, up to two character assets, no character assets with extensions, and an image reference that must match target size.
claims.boundary: The page also states human-likeness character uploads and input images containing human faces are blocked under the cited policy state.

sources.title: Video generation in the Gemini API

claims.paraphrase: Gemini Omni Flash accepts text, image, audio and video inputs and supports multi-turn editing examples such as element replacement and perspective changes.
claims.boundary: Vendor quality adjectives on the same page are not recorded as capabilities.

claims.paraphrase: Veo 3.1 is documented for native-audio video generation with extension, frame-specific generation and image-based direction through generateContent.
claims.boundary: Exact limits must come from the current endpoint schema.

claims.paraphrase: The documentation navigation exposes first-frame, first-and-last-frame, ingredients/reference-image, extension, object insertion and object removal workflows.
claims.boundary: Navigation presence identifies official workflow pages; it does not imply every model supports every workflow.

claims.paraphrase: The prompt guide recommends decomposing a video idea into key components and says not every component must appear in every prompt.
claims.boundary: Official prompting guidance, not a deterministic result guarantee.

claims.paraphrase: The guide separately defines subject, action, scene/context, camera, lighting and audio-related prompt controls.
claims.boundary: Keywords guide generation but do not prove physical lens or timing accuracy.

claims.paraphrase: Public oEmbed metadata confirms an official Google video titled 'Veo 3.1 - Frames to video'.
claims.boundary: The video content has not yet been transcript/frame distilled; it supplies no parameter claim.

claims.paraphrase: The API surface lists image-to-video, text-to-video, video-to-video, video upscale and character-control operations.
claims.boundary: Specific model support must be checked per endpoint.

claims.paraphrase: The API surface also lists sound effects, speech-to-speech, text-to-speech, dubbing, voice isolation, task management and realtime sessions.
claims.boundary: Listing is not a quality or latency guarantee.

claims.paraphrase: The current model table differentiates text/image/video inputs and lists multiple generated-video model routes rather than one universal video model.
claims.boundary: Model roster is highly version-sensitive and must be re-read at compile time.

claims.paraphrase: The page documents a creative video upscaler endpoint with an input-video maximum of 30 seconds.
claims.boundary: Applies only to the named endpoint/model on the accessed page.

claims.paraphrase: Audio models are listed separately for speech, effects, isolation, dubbing and speech-to-speech.
claims.boundary: Availability and pricing remain model-specific.

sources.title: Gen-4 Image to Video | Runway Academy

claims.paraphrase: Public oEmbed metadata confirms a Runway Academy tutorial titled 'Gen-4 Image to Video'.
claims.boundary: The video has not yet been transcript/frame distilled; it supplies no current API parameter claim.

claims.paraphrase: The page names ray-2 and ray-flash-2 and shows text-to-video plus image keyframe requests.
claims.boundary: Examples are schema evidence, not output-quality evidence.

claims.paraphrase: The API examples expose frame0, frame1, combined start/end keyframes, loop, aspect ratio, resolution and duration fields.
claims.evidence_locator: start frame, ending frame, start and end keyframes
claims.boundary: Allowed values remain current-schema facts.

claims.paraphrase: Extension is documented only for completed videos generated by the service, and the page directs clients to a concepts-list endpoint rather than inventing motion tokens.
claims.boundary: Does not establish subjective camera quality.

sources.title: Generate video with Firefly models and add it to the timeline

claims.paraphrase: Generated videos are saved to Generation History and can be dragged onto the Firefly editor timeline.
claims.boundary: Proves editor workflow, not model output quality.

claims.paraphrase: The public page exposes model choice and timeline insertion but does not publish a stable numeric model version.
claims.boundary: Numeric model version remains unknown.

claims.paraphrase: Availability can vary by geographic location, user type, regulation and plan.
claims.boundary: Access must be checked in the user's account rather than assumed.

claims.paraphrase: An input image may be center-cropped to the model's required size, potentially losing edge content.
claims.boundary: Pre-crop critical compositions before generation.

claims.paraphrase: Using the same seed, prompt and controls can generate a similar asset; changing properties changes the experiment.
claims.boundary: Similar is not identical or deterministic.

sources.title: Generate videos using Kling video generation model

claims.paraphrase: The page documents Kling 2.5 Turbo plus Kling 3.0 and Kling 3.0 Omni inside Firefly; a first frame is mandatory for the described Kling workflows.
claims.boundary: Applies to the Firefly integration, not the underlying provider API.

claims.paraphrase: Kling 3.0 and 3.0 Omni allow a maximum total duration of 15 seconds and per-shot duration control.
claims.boundary: Current Firefly UI limit at access date.

claims.paraphrase: The page documents synchronized audio, a multi-shot toggle with up to five shots, and element references created from images or video.
claims.boundary: Does not prove identity consistency or audio quality.

claims.paraphrase: The page states that Kling access is for individual subscribers rather than Teams or Enterprise creators.
claims.boundary: Plan availability can change and must be rechecked.
